chunks: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ja'far al-Alawi al-Hasani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ali b. Khalaf al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Hasan b. Salih b. Abi al-Aswad narrated to us. He said: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us from Muhammad b. Qays. He said:

When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) would come back from a journey, he would begin with Fatima (peace be upon her). So, he would visit her, and he would prolong his stay. Once, he went out on a journey, and Fatima (peace be upon her) made two silver bracelets, a necklace, two earrings, and a curtain for the door of the house, in preparation for the arrival of her father and her husband (peace be upon them both). When the Messenger of Allah came, he visited her. His companions stood at the door, not knowing whether they should wait or leave due to his prolonged stay with her. So, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went out to them. Anger could be seen on his face, and he sat at the pulpit. Fatima (peace be upon her) thought that the Messenger of Allah had only done that because of what he had seen of the bracelets, necklace, earrings, and curtain. So she removed her necklace, earrings, and bracelets, and took down the curtain.

She sent them to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and said to the messenger: 'Say to him: Your daughter sends her greetings to you and says: Put this toward the cause of Allah.' When he came to him and informed him, he (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'She has done it - may her father be her ransom' - three times - 'This world is not of Muhammad nor of the Family of Muhammad. Had this world been worth the value of a wing of a mosquito before Allah in goodness, He would not have given a disbeliever a drink of water from it.' Then he stood and went to visit her.

key_terms.جَنَاحَ بَعُوضَةٍ: A wing of a mosquito - proverbial expression for utter worthlessness
key_terms.فِدَاهَا أَبُوهَا: May her father be her ransom - an expression of extreme paternal affection and pride
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ: In the cause/way of Allah - giving for charitable or religious purposes
key_terms.مَسْكَتَيْنِ: Two bracelets - silver arm bands worn as adornment

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about Fatima removing her jewelry for the cause of Allah?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts how Fatima al-Zahra prepared jewelry and decorations for the Prophet's return from a journey. When the Prophet showed displeasure, Fatima immediately sent all her ornaments to him for the cause of Allah. The Prophet's response - repeating 'may her father be her ransom' three times and declaring the worthlessness of the material world - reveals both his pride in Fatima's spiritual detachment and his teaching about the insignificance of worldly possessions.
word_analysis: may her father be her ransom

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa`id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Ja`far al-`Alawi al-Hasani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Ali b. Khalaf al-`Attar narrated to us. He said: Hasan b. Salih b. Abi’l Aswad narrated to us. He said: Abu Mu`shar narrated to us from Muhammad b. Qays.  He said:

When the Prophet (s) would come back from a journey, he would begin with Fatima (sa). So, he would visit her, and he would prolong his stay. Once, he went out on a journey, and Fatima (sa) wore two silver bracelets, necklaces, earrings, and a tunic. She waited at the door of the house in preparation for the arrival of her father and her husband (as). When the Messenger of Allah (s) came, he visited her. His companions stood at the door, not knowing whether they should wait there or leave, due to his prolonged stay with her. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) went out to them. Anger could be seen on his face as he went forth and sat on the pulpit. Fatima (sa) thought that the Messenger of Allah (s) had done that because of what he had seen of her bracelets, necklaces, earrings, and tunic. So, she removed her bracelets, necklaces, earrings, and tunic, and sent for [a messenger] to bring them to the Messenger of Allah (s). She said to the messenger: Say to him (s): “Your daughter recites the salaam to you and says: put these toward the Cause of Allah.”

When he came to him and informed him, he (s) said: Her father has fulfilled her sacrifice – three times. This world is not of Muhammad nor the Family of Muhammad. Had this world been worth the value of a wing of a mosquito to Allah, He would not have fed a disbeliever water from it. Then, he went and visited her.
